A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTUITOR/RLIF research. All 30 pages of v2 and 39 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated background, experiments and examples can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark results, training trajectories and ablations, including Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–12.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds reward, optimization, rollout-size and staged-training experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The core self-certainty reward and group-normalized GRPO procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B.7 adds experimental adaptations that equally mix INTUITOR and GRPO advantages or train with INTUITOR before switching to GRPO. v2 discussed combining reward signals only as future work.

E1.justification: All named training and evaluation datasets and task families are retained. Appendix B.10 newly discusses noisy or incomplete questions and recovery on cleaner data, but does not clearly distinguish separately performed evaluations from illustrative failure discussion. Whether this adds an evaluated input scenario is uncertain.

E2.justification: v3 substantially expands evaluated alternatives with raw and length-normalized log-probability rewards, direct self-certainty optimization, and mixed or staged INTUITOR/GRPO training (B.4–B.7). Table 5 also adds GRPO-PV to the Llama3.2-3B-Instruct comparison. The original GRPO, plurality-voting, entropy and random-reward comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a two-epoch Qwen2.5-3B entropy comparison, a 7-versus-14 rollout-size experiment, matched two-epoch GRPO versus INTUITOR-to-GRPO schedules, sequential Codeforces-to-MATH training, and a Llama3.2-3B-Base failure test. These extend experimental settings; the retained main protocol and hyperparameter table are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds substantial analyses of longer-run entropy degeneration, log-probability rewards, direct optimization, rollout-size sensitivity, reward combination, sequential domain training, correctness variance and failure conditions. These address additional questions about reward choice, optimization stability and applicability. The earlier KL, scaling, architecture and online-versus-offline analyses are retained.

E5.justification: B.9 and Figure 16 add within-group and across-completion standard deviations of correctness during training. This introduces response-level dispersion reporting, not uncertainty across independent training runs. The existing Mann–Whitney U tests, p-values and effect sizes remain unchanged; neither version specifies independent-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: The main benchmark results remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial result entries and trajectories. New settings yield GSM8K/MATH500 scores of 0.814/0.644 with 14 rollouts, 0.838/0.672 for INTUITOR-to-GRPO training, and 0.808/0.644 for Codeforces-to-MATH training. Table 5 adds Llama GRPO-PV results. Table 8 reports GRPO GSM8K as 0.836 while Table 1 retains 0.826; this unexplained discrepancy does not establish a corrected same-setting score.

T1.justification: B.4 and B.7 add mathematical definitions of raw and normalized log-probability rewards and the mixed advantage, including reasoning about sequence-length bias. The core self-certainty and GRPO formulations are retained, while RLHF/RLVR objectives move to Appendix A. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The contribution list and conclusion narrow the claim of superior out-of-domain generalization to competitive, sometimes better generalization. The central claims about learning without external rewards, comparable mathematical performance and emergent structured reasoning remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability boundaries: adequate prior knowledge, suitable prompts/data and careful hyperparameters are necessary, and confidence need not reflect correctness (B.10). It adds explanations for alternative-reward collapse and staged-training benefits, and acknowledges no stronger correctness-variance reduction than GRPO. Section 6 newly identifies unresolved theoretical mechanisms and reasoning boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 documents settings for new studies, including equal advantage mixing, epoch schedules and a failed 7B learning rate, and adds reproducibility guidance. Existing prompts, GPU information, repository link and the hyperparameter table are retained. The explicit sampled KL-penalty formula shown in v2's method section is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations concerning SRT, the generation–verification gap, sharpening, spurious rewards and RLVR reasoning limits. It removes the AlphaGo Zero historical reference. These refine the existing intrinsic-feedback positioning without redefining the central novelty claim; publication updates and the consolidated Qwen reference are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 moves external-feedback background to Appendix A and KL analysis to B.1, merges model-family subsections, introduces explicit research questions, revises parts of the discussion and captions, and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 13–16 and Tables 7–9, expands Table 5, relocates the KL table to the appendix and places Figures 3 and 4 side by side. The conference format changes headers, typography, table styling and page composition throughout. Original figure graphics and completion examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The new longer-run entropy comparison and direct-optimization controls substantially strengthen the justification for using self-certainty through policy gradients; v2's alternative-reward evidence was limited to early entropy collapse and random rewards. Explicit failure conditions, negative variance findings and narrower generalization claims also make the paper's conclusions better qualified. Table 8's unexplained GRPO score discrepancy weakens that particular comparison, but does not outweigh the stronger evidence about the method's design and boundaries.
